question.problem: The vector $a$ is directed due north-west and $|\,a\,|=5$, while the vector $b$ is directed due south-west and $|\,b\,|=12.$ Which of the following is a unit vector that is parallel to $a+b?$

current_example.problem: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ is directed horizontally to the right and has magnitude $10,$ while the vector $\mathbf{b}$ is directed vertically down and has magnitude $20.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{a+b}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we have to find $\mathbf{a+b}.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ goes from the tail of $\mathbf{a}$ to the head of $\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251721/assets/32c48d8c19fc68fbc172b240ded922f3e2ebc12804411c318ff63fe999aaedcc.png)

To find the unit vector corresponding to $\mathbf{a+b},$ we have to divide by the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the magnitude, first notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}{|a+b|}^{2} & ={|a|}^{2}+{|b|}^{2} \\  & ={10}^{2}+{20}^{2} \\  & =100+400 \\  & =500\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude is

$$
|\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{500}=10\sqrt{5},
$$

and the corresponding unit vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{10\sqrt{5}}(a+b).\end{aligned}
$$
